Hello! I'm a fourth-year PhD candidate in the Political Analysis track of
Harvard University's PhD Program in Health Policy.

My research examines how the design and implementation of health insurance
programs shape both coverage and access outcomes, and people's experiences with
government. I'm particularly interested in how those experiences, in turn,
shape political attitudes and behavior. Most of my work focuses on the Medicaid
and Medicare programs, as well as the Affordable Care Act's Marketplaces. I use
large administrative and survey datasets alongside quasi-experimental methods
to study these questions.

I'm also interested in teaching and in helping students connect questions about
public policy and politics to broader questions about institutions, power, and
inequality.

Before graduate school,
I worked as a Program Assistant for the Health Care Coverage and Access team at
the Commonwealth Fund and as a Special Assistant to the Assistant Secretary for
Legislation at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services during the
summer of 2022.

I have a Master in Public Policy from the Harvard Kennedy School (2023), and a
BS in Public Health through the Department of Health Policy and Management from
UNC-Chapel Hill (2019).
